title: Greeting bot

blocks.md:
## Keep the bot

A reusable greeting is a function that returns a string, not a one-off print. `greet(name)` should hand back `Hello, Ada!` when a name is present, and `Hello!` when the name is empty. The two `print` calls below the function are already there. They show what the function returned, so your job is the return value, not a second copy of the output.

This bites when you only `print` inside `greet` and return nothing. Then `print(greet("Ada"))` prints the greeting and also `None`, so the checked output no longer matches. Empty input is the other trap: treating `""` like a real name produces the broken line `Hello, !`.

```python
def greet(name):
    if not name:
        return "Hello!"
    return f"Hello, {name}!"
```

A common mistake is hardcoding both lines or forgetting the empty-name branch. The exercise asks you to return the two exact strings so the existing prints show `Hello, Ada!` then `Hello!`.

hintLadder.md: Return a value. The prints are already there.
if not name: return "Hello!" else return f"Hello, {name}!"
